preamble: Palatalization of the voiced velar stop [g] to the voiced alveolo-palatal affricate [dʑ] before front vowels and glides, without devoicing. It is characteristic of Wu Chinese, which keeps the Middle Chinese voiced (murmured) obstruents: Middle Chinese 群 [g] before [i, y] is [dʑ] in Shanghainese, Suzhounese, Hangzhou, Ningbo and most other Wu varieties, whereas Mandarin and New Xiang devoiced it to [tɕ] or [tɕʰ].

examples.note: Wu retains the voiced initial while palatalizing it before the front glide.
Synchronic allophony: Wiktionary gives Asante Twi [dʑe]; Wikipedia's allophone table gives /ɡ/ as [ɡ, dʑ~ɟʝ]. Christaller notes that gɛ, ge, gi do not occur, only gye, gyi.
Cited by Adomako (2018). The affricates go back to a diachronic palatalization of velars, and the rule is now largely unproductive.

sources: Norman, J. (1988). Chinese. Cambridge University Press. https://www.cambridge.org/9780521296533
